title: ATM state machine and flows
idea: The ATM lifecycle is a state machine: the machine is in exactly one ATMState, and only listed transitions are allowed, so no step can be skipped.
points: IDLE goes to CARD_INSERTED; a correct PIN moves it to AUTHENTICATED.
Only AUTHENTICATED may enter DISPENSING; it ends at IDLE, or OUT_OF_SERVICE on a jam.
Three wrong PINs retain the card and return the machine to IDLE.
A jam or empty cassette sends it OUT_OF_SERVICE until an operator resets it.

messages.label: insert card
messages.note: The machine moves IDLE to CARD_INSERTED and asks for a PIN.

messages.label: verifyPin(card, pin)
messages.note: The bank checks the PIN and counts failures. The ATM never stores PINs.

messages.label: ok, AC-1
messages.note: Success moves the machine to AUTHENTICATED.

messages.label: withdraw 2600
messages.note: The ATM plans notes first. If they cannot make 2600, it refuses here.

messages.label: debit(AC-1, 2600, R-1)
messages.note: R-1 is the request id. A retry with R-1 cannot debit twice.

messages.label: TX-1 PENDING
messages.note: Page 3's one-step debit now becomes two: the money is held PENDING until the cash really leaves.

messages.label: dispense(plan)
messages.note: The machine moves to DISPENSING and pushes the notes out.

messages.label: confirm(TX-1)
messages.note: Notes taken: TX-1 becomes COMPLETED. A jam would send reverse(TX-1) instead.

messages.label: card back
messages.note: The card is returned and the machine is IDLE again.

code.title: ATMState with rules
code.caption: The allowed moves live in the enum. ATM asks the enum before every change.

walk.text: Dispensing with no card is refused before anything else happens.
One wrong PIN, then a right one, a withdrawal, and back to IDLE.
The next customer fails the PIN three times; the card is kept.
The cassette runs out. No new card is accepted until a reset.
An `EnumMap` lists the allowed next states; `canMoveTo` asks it.
`moveTo` is the only way to change state, so illegal moves are refused in one place.
The third wrong PIN retains the card and returns to IDLE.

pitfalls: Do not set `state` from many methods; route every change through `moveTo`.
Count PIN failures at the bank too; a local count resets at the next ATM.
Keep ATMState and TransactionStatus separate; a jam changes both for different reasons.

quiz.q: What does the last line of AtmLifecycle print?
quiz.why: OUT_OF_SERVICE may only move to IDLE. `canMoveTo` returns false, so `moveTo` prints the refusal and keeps the state.

takeaway: One enum lists the legal moves; one method makes every move.

starters: Should I use the State pattern with one class per state instead?
What happens if the customer walks away during DISPENSING?
How does the ATM recover its state after a power cut?
